primary.summary_en: The Feast of Saints Simon and Jude, Apostles, is celebrated on October 28. It honors two of the original twelve disciples of Jesus Christ, traditionally commemorated together due to early Christian traditions linking their martyrdoms.
primary.body_en: Saint Simon, often called the Zealot or the Cananean, is distinguished from Simon Peter in the Gospel lists, though little biographical detail is recorded. Tradition suggests he preached in Egypt and Persia before being martyred. Saint Jude, also known as Thaddeus, is the author of the Epistle of Jude and is patron of hopeless cases. The liturgy for this Feast emphasizes the unity of the apostolic mission and the foundation of the Church upon the apostles and prophets, as described in the first reading from Ephesians 2:19-22, which declares the faithful as fellow citizens with the holy ones and members of the household of God.
primary.confidence_note_en: This is the fixed celebration on the General Roman Calendar as listed in the USCCB 2026 Liturgical Calendar.
